Despite these concerns, an IOCL representative denied any plans for relocation.

recent_articles.title: The Simple living in Kurma Gramam village - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Kurma Gramam**, a village in Andhra Pradesh, is an isolated community that has embraced a traditional lifestyle. Residents live without electricity, mobile phones, or internet access, relying on simple practices like hand-woven clothing and traditional food.  The village follows a disciplined routine with daily prayers and discourses on the Bhagavad Gita and Bhagavatam. **Srikanth**, a B. Tech graduate who moved to the village in 2019, teaches Vedic knowledge to children. Visitors are welcomed but encouraged to leave no plastic behind. The village thrives on simplicity and spiritual discipline.

recent_articles.title: Sharan Prakash Patil takes umbrage at remarks by BJP leaders against Mallikarjun Kharge - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Dr. Sharan Prakash Patil**, **Medical Education Minister**, criticized **BJP leaders** for making "irresponsible" and "disrespectful" remarks against **AICC president Mallikarjun Kharge**.  Patil condemned the comments, arguing that they are being blown out of proportion and comparing them to past instances of similar attacks by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on Congress leaders. He also questioned the basis for comparisons made by **Union Home Minister Amit Shah** against **Jawaharlal Nehru**, emphasizing the Congress's commitment to non-alignment and condemnation of aggression without supporting war.

recent_articles.title: National politics yet regional sentiment - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**'s letter to **Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi** on the occasion of Utkal Dibas (Odisha Day) sparked political debate.  Modi praised the late socialist leader **Biju Patnaik**, highlighting his dedication to nation-building and inspiring qualities.

recent_articles.title: Odisha Law Commission recommends a new law on hate speech, hate crime - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **The Odisha State Law Commission** has recommended the creation of a new law to combat hate speech and crimes.  The commission, led by retired **Justice Biswanath Rath**, took suo motu cognizance of the need for such legislation after observing an increase in hate speech on social media and other public platforms. The matter was referred to a sub-committee in January 2026.

recent_articles.title: Sasmit Patra offers to quit as BJD Parliamentary Party leader in Rajya Sabha - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: **Sasmit Patra**, a two-time Rajya Sabha member, has submitted his resignation as leader of the **Biju Janata Dal (BJD)** in the Upper House to **Naveen Patnaik**. The move is expected to pave the way for another MP to take over the leadership position.  Patra's decision comes after **Santrupt Misra**, a political advisor to **Patnaik**, took oath as a Rajya Sabha member on Monday following his election victory. The BJD currently has six members in the Rajya Sabha and faces challenges with no representation in the Lok Sabha after losing seats in the 2024 general election.

recent_articles.title: States to be pushed for ‘utility led aggregation’ to meet PM Surya Ghar targets - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Ministry of New and Renewable Energy (MNRE)** is seeking to boost the adoption of its **PM Surya Ghar** program, which aims to provide solar energy access to one crore households by March 2027. The MNRE is encouraging states to adopt a “utility-led aggregation (ULA)” model where electricity distribution companies will pay for rooftop solar installations in eligible households.  The program has seen limited uptake but the MNRE is proposing incentives to increase participation. Despite this, India's renewable energy growth was significant in 2025-26, adding 55.3 gigawatts of non-fossil capacity, with solar power accounting for 44.6 GW.

recent_articles.title: Several villagers, police personnel injured in clash in Odisha amid protests against mining of bauxite - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: A clash erupted in Odisha's Rayagada district on Tuesday between villagers and police, resulting in injuries to both sides. **Vedanta Limited**, the company seeking to mine bauxite at Sijimali, has been accused of securing fraudulent forest clearance and pressuring the government for mining despite opposition from local communities.  **Tribal communities** have protested against the project, claiming it will harm their livelihood and water sources. Police used lathi charge and tear gas shells to disperse villagers who pelted stones, injuring 58 personnel, while activists allege police assaulted villagers to deter them from opposing the project.

recent_articles.title: Assam Assembly election 2026: Curtains down on high-voltage campaign - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly elections concluded on April 7, with voters casting their ballots for the state's 126 seats. **Prime Minister Narendra Modi**, **Union Home Minister Amit Shah**, and other BJP leaders campaigned against the opposition Congress, accusing it of promoting infiltrators and failing to address development issues. The Congress countered by highlighting corruption allegations against the ruling party and promising justice for singer Zubeen Garg if elected. Prominent candidates include Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma, Gaurav Gogoi (Congress), Badruddin Ajmal (AIUDF), and Debabrata Saikia (opposition).  The elections will be held in a single phase on April 9th.

recent_articles.title: Assembly elections 2026: ECI may roll out SIR in remaining 17 States, 5 UTs post polls - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The **Election Commission** is considering rolling out the third and final phase of Special Intensive Revision (SIR) for voters' lists in 22 states and Union territories after the Assembly elections this month. The exercise, which aims to clean up electoral rolls, could begin after the polls conclude on April 29th or after the declaration of results.  The **Election Commission** has already conducted SIR in 10 states and three Union Territories, covering nearly 60 crore voters.

recent_articles.title: Assam election verdict hinges on parties reading the tea leaves right - The Hindu
recent_articles.rephrased_article: The Assam Assembly election campaign is being heavily influenced by the tea tribe community, which comprises almost 20% of voters.  **Rahul Gandhi**, leader of the **Congress**, promised daily wages of ₹450 and Scheduled Tribe status for six communities, including tea tribes, while **Hemant Soren**, Jharkhand Chief Minister, campaigned for a candidate from the **Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM)**, highlighting the lack of ST status for these communities in Assam.  The BJP is promising land rights to over 3.5 lakh families and raising minimum wages to ₹500. The JMM's entry into the race has complicated matters for both major parties, but its impact on the tea tribe vote remains uncertain.
